concerns.text: Task T057 and T058 are marked as incomplete (checkbox unchecked). These tasks are required to verify the final title audit and methodology consistency, which are critical for satisfying the 'Richard Feynman' review response and the Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) regarding the project title. Without these tasks being executable, the plan cannot satisfy the spec's requirement to resolve the 'First-Principles' contradiction.

Task T060 is marked as incomplete. This task is the only mechanism defined to physically amend the Constitution title (FR-030) from 'First-Principles' to 'Surrogate Model'. The Analyze report flags this as a CRITICAL governance conflict. If T060 is not executed, the Constitution remains in direct contradiction to the Spec and Plan, violating the Single Source of Truth principle.

Task T009a mandates a runtime source enforcement lock file (`data/.source_state`), but the dependent tasks (T013d1 download, T013d0_final orchestration) do not explicitly include the logic to create, manage, or clean up this lock file. The spec US1 requires a 'single canonical source' constraint. Without a task explicitly implementing the lock file lifecycle, the constraint cannot be enforced, leaving SC-001 (single source) unverified.

Spec SC-004 requires 'Peak memory usage during training remains within acceptable system limits'. Task T008a tests memory for the *data loading pipeline* only. Task T018c enforces memory *during training* but does not verify the *combined* peak memory (loading + training) of a full end-to-end run. There is no task defined to run a full end-to-end cycle to verify the aggregate peak memory stays under 7GB as implied by the success criterion.

Task T023 and T024 include a note stating 'The iteration count (1000) is a placeholder; tune based on runtime'. This introduces ambiguity into the verification of SC-005 (p < 0.05). While the task exists, the lack of a fixed, verifiable threshold in the task description makes the success criterion non-deterministic and potentially untestable as written.
